lab_title: Human Heart Anatomy and Blood Flow Pathway AR Lab
top_level_objectives: Identify the four heart chambers, four valves, and major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the complete path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Explain how valve positions support one-way blood flow and prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to the different pressure demands of pulmonary versus systemic circulation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heart as a three-dimensional organ and establish anatomical orientation before moving inside.
key_visuals: Life-sized 3D heart model in anterior view
Labels for apex, base, anterior surface, right/left sides from the patient perspective
Major vessels visible at the superior aspect of the heart
student_actions: Rotate or walk around the heart to distinguish anterior/posterior and patient right/left orientation.
Tap highlighted surface landmarks and major vessel openings to reveal brief orientation notes.

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students identify the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle and understand their spatial relationships.
key_visuals: Heart opened in a frontal cutaway
Four chambers color-tinted with labels
Interatrial and interventricular septa visible between right and left sides
student_actions: Select each chamber in sequence and match it to its name.
Compare atria versus ventricles by location, size, and wall thickness.

scenes.scene_name: 3. Major Vessels Entering and Leaving the Heart
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect each chamber to the vessels that bring blood into or carry blood away from the heart.
key_visuals: Superior vena cava and inferior vena cava entering the right atrium
Pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries leaving the right ventricle
Pulmonary veins entering the left atrium
Aorta leaving the left ventricle
student_actions: Trace vessel-to-chamber connections using guided highlights.
Sort the vessels into inflow vessels and outflow vessels.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the four valves and show how they separate chambers or vessels to maintain directional flow.
key_visuals: Close-up cutaway of tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, and aortic valves
Valve leaflets shown opening and closing
Simple arrows indicating allowed blood flow direction
student_actions: Tap each valve to identify its location and name.
Predict whether each valve is open or closed during filling or ejection phases.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the right-side pathway from systemic venous return through the heart to the pulmonary circuit.
key_visuals: Blue flow particles entering through the superior and inferior vena cava
Pathway through right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary arteries
Lung icons or simplified pulmonary capillary beds beyond the heart
student_actions: Follow the blue blood-flow trail step by step and name each structure it passes through.
Place pathway checkpoints in the correct order from body return to lungs.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the left-side pathway from pulmonary venous return through the heart to systemic circulation.
key_visuals: Red flow particles returning from lungs through pulmonary veins
Pathway through left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta
Systemic circulation icon or branching arteries beyond the aorta
student_actions: Follow the red blood-flow trail and identify each chamber, valve, and vessel in sequence.
Complete a combined dual-loop pathway map from vena cava to aorta.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain why the left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle.
key_visuals: Cross-section comparing right and left ventricular wall thickness
Pressure or distance indicators for pulmonary versus systemic circuits
Animated contraction showing stronger left ventricular ejection into the aorta
student_actions: Measure or compare ventricular wall thickness visually using AR guides.
Answer a prompt linking wall thickness to the distance and resistance of the circuit being served.

scenes.scene_name: 8. Integrated Challenge: Trace and Explain Flow
scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate anatomy identification, blood-flow sequence, valve function, and ventricular structure into one applied review.
key_visuals: Unlabeled cutaway heart with optional color-coded flow toggles
Interactive pathway arrows hidden until requested
Checklist of chambers, valves, and vessels to identify
student_actions: Label the major chambers, valves, and vessels on the unlabeled model.
Trace the full blood pathway aloud or by selecting structures in order.
Explain where valves prevent backflow and why the left ventricle is thicker than the right.
